targetText: big industry, and the limitless expansion of production which it makes possible, bring within the range of feasibility a social order in which so much is produced that every member of society will be in a position to exercise and develop all his powers and faculties in complete freedom.
explanation: Replacing competitive private ownership with democratic social planning resolves the structural contradiction between collective industrial production and private appropriation.

targetText: for big industry, competition and generally the individualistic organization of production have become a fetter which it must and will shatter; that so long as big industry remains on its present footing, it can be maintained only through the general chaos of every seven years, each time threatening the whole of civilization and not only plunging the proletarians into misery but also ruining large sections of the bourgeoisie; hence either that big industry must itself be given up, which is an absolute impossibility, or that it makes unavoidably necessary an entirely new organization of society in which production is no longer directed by mutually competing individual industrialists but rather by the whole society operating according to a definite plan and according to the needs of all.
summary: The individualistic organization of production has become a fetter: replacing competitive chaos with societal planning.
explanation: Engels explains that large-scale mechanized industry cannot function sustainably under the anarchy of individualistic competition and private ownership, which repeatedly produces devastating periodic crises. Industry unavoidably requires replacing individualistic direction with collective social planning for the needs of all.
context: Question 13: What were the consequences of the industrial revolution and dividing society into bourgeoisie and proletariat?
